correctness.rationale: The integral toric semigroup is saturated, the four maximal minors have absolute values 1,n,1,1, and mod p|n leaves three monomial Newton vertices. Saturation gives an explicit four-generator character cone; dual facets yield four primitive cocharacter rays. Rank-two lattice indices, singular-orbit counts, and rational canonical support equations are derived for all n. The embedded standard-library checker recomputes these identities independently for 2<=n<=512, but the proof does not extrapolate from finite tests.

value.rationale: The fixed exponent-two example is an important obstruction to one-step Nash resolution; extending it to every triple-axis cover w^n=abc is a canonical mathematical test family. The theorem detects the structural boundary between isolated and one-dimensional singular strata and a sharp canonical-divisor phase diagram modulo 2 and 3. These are intrinsic invariants pertinent to resolutions and minimal-model questions, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
